sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 of the August 1930 Sanborn atlas of Audubon, New Jersey, covering the northern part of the Borough of Oaklyn, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The sheet spans the blocks between Lake Newton on the west and East Clinton Avenue on the east, from the shore of Lake Newton and Oaklawn Avenue at the top down to North White Horse Pike along the bottom edge. Cross streets are Oaklawn Avenue, Cold Springs Avenue and Johnson Avenue; the north-south streets are East Lakeview, East Beechwood, East Bettlewood, East Haddon and East Clinton Avenues, with East Bettlewood Avenue continuing north to the lake shore as a diagonal road. Johnson Avenue is offset where it crosses East Beechwood Avenue. The area is almost entirely residential: frame dwellings on narrow lots, with rows of brick-veneered houses along Oaklawn Avenue and East Haddon Avenue, and a few garages. Named buildings are the Blackiston Apartments and De Chavanne Apartments on Johnson Avenue blocks, the Oaklyn Baptist Church with its Sunday school, St. Mark's Lutheran Church, and gasoline stations facing the pike. The western third of the sheet is open water of Lake Newton with the borough line between Collingswood and Oaklyn drawn through it, and the line between Haddon Township and the Borough of Oaklyn runs along the north edge. Water pipes, fire hydrants and fire alarm boxes are marked along the streets. The street names of the next sheet (sheet 10) are lettered in the margin below the pike, and the adjoining sheet numbers 5, 10 and 11 are printed at the edges.
notes: Cold Springs Av. is Coldsprings Avenue in OpenStreetMap; E. Lakeview Av. is East Lakeview Drive; N. White Horse Pike is White Horse Pike.
Oaklawn Avenue / East Bettlewood Avenue (a skewed multi-street junction) was excluded: detected 4 m off the fit.

Map. Audubon series sheet 4 (Oaklyn), 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper left (rotation about -58 deg). Oaklawn, Cold Springs and Johnson Avs between E. Beechwood and E. Clinton Avs; Lake Newton on the west; N. White Horse Pike along the bottom edge. One part.

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 of the August 1930 Sanborn atlas of Audubon, New Jersey, covering the western part of the Borough of Oaklyn south of North White Horse Pike, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The sheet runs from the pike at the top to Kendall Boulevard and Washington Avenue at the bottom, and from the shore of Newton Lake on the west to West Clinton Avenue on the east. North-south streets are West Lakeview, West Beechwood, West Bettlewood, West Haddon and West Clinton Avenues and Hillcrest Avenue; cross streets are Newton Avenue, Manheim Avenue, Reading Avenue, Manor Avenue, Woodland Terrace and Kendall Boulevard, with Goff Avenue running diagonally to the south. The Philadelphia and Reading Railway, Atlantic City division, crosses the sheet on a diagonal between Reading and Manor Avenues, and a trolley right of way crosses the blocks west of West Lakeview Avenue, which is marked not opened. The area is residential, with long rows of frame dwellings along Newton, Reading and Manor Avenues. Named buildings near the pike include the Lu-George Apartments, a vacant concrete-floored building, a Roman Catholic church, a private hospital and a gasoline station; a bowling alley stands on West Clinton Avenue and a sewerage pumping plant on Goff Avenue. The western and southern margins show Newton Lake with lots running to the shore. Street names of sheet 4 are lettered above the pike.
notes: The railroad is lettered P. & R. R'y (A.C. Div'n), the Philadelphia and Reading line to Atlantic City; OpenStreetMap names it Beesleys Point Secondary.
W. Lakeview Av. is West Lakeview Drive in OpenStreetMap; N. White Horse Pike is White Horse Pike.
Kendall Boulevard / West Clinton Avenue was excluded on this sheet: only the corner is drawn, at the sheet edge.

Map. Audubon series sheet 10 (Oaklyn), 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper left. N. White Horse Pike (top) to Kendall Blvd, W. Lakeview to W. Clinton Avs; Newton, Manheim, Reading, Manor Avs, Woodland Ter, Goff Av; P.R.R. Atlantic City division crossing diagonally; Newton Lake on the west. One part.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 of the August 1930 Sanborn atlas of Audubon, New Jersey, covering the eastern part of the Borough of Oaklyn south of North White Horse Pike, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. It runs from the pike at the top to Peter Creek at the bottom, and from West Clinton Avenue on the west to West Holly Avenue on the east. North-south streets are West Clinton, West Collingswood, West Greenwood, West Oakland and West Holly Avenues; cross streets are Newton Avenue, Manheim Avenue, Manor Avenue and Sylvan Avenue, and south of the railroad a diagonal grid of Kendall Boulevard, Landis, Bryant and Walnut Avenues and the southern part of West Oakland Avenue. The Philadelphia and Reading Railway, Atlantic City division, crosses on a diagonal with Oaklyn Station beside Manheim Avenue. Along the pike and Newton Avenue are the Oaklyn Borough Hall and Welcome Fire Company, a first Oaklyn Public School, gasoline stations, an auto service station and a garage; the fire department of Oaklyn Fire Co. No. 1 and the planing mill and lumber sheds of the Suburban Lumber Co. stand by the railroad. South of the railroad are a large garage on West Clinton Avenue, a golf course, and a new fireproof Oaklyn Public School built in 1925 near Kendall Boulevard. The rest is frame dwellings, with large open blocks east of West Oakland Avenue. The boundary between Haddon Township and the Borough of Oaklyn follows the pike, and the margin above it names the streets of sheets 4 and 5.
notes: Sylvan Av. east of West Oakland Avenue is now part of Kendall Boulevard in OpenStreetMap.
The railroad is lettered P. & R. R'y (A.C. Div'n); OpenStreetMap names it Beesleys Point Secondary.
Kendall Boulevard / West Clinton Avenue is drawn with rounded corners; the detector placed it about 30 ft off, so it was hand-picked.
The creek is lettered Peter Creek here and Peters Creek on sheet 16.

Map. Audubon series sheet 11 (Oaklyn), 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper left. N. White Horse Pike to Peters Creek, W. Clinton to W. Holly Avs; Newton, Manheim, Manor, Sylvan Avs, Kendall Blvd, Landis, Bryant, Walnut, W. Oakland Avs; Oaklyn station on the P.R.R. One part.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 of the August 1930 Sanborn atlas of Audubon, New Jersey, covering the southwestern corner of the Borough of Oaklyn, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. The sheet shows the tongue of land between Newton Lake on the north and Peters Creek on the west, from the Black Horse Pike bridge at the upper left corner to Washington Avenue and West Clinton Avenue at the bottom. Kendall Boulevard enters from the pike, curves across the top of the sheet and runs south along its east side; inside it lie Harding Avenue, which bends from an east-west street into a north-south one, Eden Avenue, Ridgeway Avenue, Goff Avenue and Washington Avenue. The area is a recent residential subdivision of narrow lots, many still vacant, with rows of small frame dwellings along Ridgeway, Harding and Eden Avenues and a few on Kendall Boulevard near the lake. No industry or institutions are shown; a corner of the Oaklyn Public School of sheet 11 appears at the bottom edge. The western half of the sheet is the marshy valley of Peters Creek, with the boundary between the Borough of Oaklyn and the Borough of Audubon drawn through it, and the shores of Newton Lake fringe the northern lots. Water pipes and hydrants are marked along the streets.
notes: Kendall Boulevard / Black Horse Pike lies just off the sheet and was not used.
The creek is lettered Peters Creek here and Peter Creek on sheet 11.
Map. Audubon series sheet 16 (Oaklyn), 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper left. Between Newton Lake and Peters Creek: Kendall Blvd, Harding, Eden, Ridgeway, Goff and Washington Avs. One part.
